questions.stem: A team wants a standard JSR 269 processor to add a missing getter to a class it finds in the sources being compiled. What does the standard API let the processor do?

options.text: Open that class's own source file through the Filer and insert the getter into it
options.says: The Filer creates new files; the page lists that a processor cannot modify existing source code through the standard API.

options.text: Rewrite that class's compiled class file once javac has written its bytecode
options.says: The page says processors can only generate new files; changing existing classes is what Lombok does through javac's internal APIs, outside the standard one.

options.text: Write a separate new source file, such as a helper or subclass, next to it
options.says: A standard processor can only generate new files, such as sources and resources; the page names this as its one way to add code.

questions.stem: In round 1 a processor writes a new source file whose class carries an annotation that another processor supports. When does that other processor see the new class?

options.text: In the next round, once javac has parsed the newly written files
options.says: Processors run in rounds, and files generated in round N are processed by processors in round N+1.

options.text: In the same round, as soon as the Filer has finished writing the file
options.says: A round works on the elements it started with; new files wait for the next round, as the page's rounds rule states.

options.text: In no round, because generated sources are compiled without processing
options.says: Generated files do take part: the page says files from round N are processed in round N+1, which is how generated code triggers further processing.
